- CLAUDE.md
  Line or code reference: Lines 1467-1469 (enforcement paragraph)
  Problem: §25.D documents that the hook "fails open with a `systemMessage` warning when the hook payload ... is invalid", but the implementation at `.claude/hooks/pr_watch_guard.py:99` (`payload = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}`) silently coerces empty and whitespace-only stdin to `{}` without emitting any warning. An empty or whitespace-only string is not valid JSON, yet no warning fires.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — the guard correctly allows the call. This is a documentation-vs-behavior precision gap: an operator reading the §25.D enforcement text could conclude every non-normal payload triggers a warning and be surprised when an empty payload produces silence. The test at `tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py:174-176` explicitly documents that empty payloads are intentionally allowed without warning.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=4

- CLAUDE.md
  Line or code reference: §25.D enforcement paragraph, lines 1464-1470 ("fails open with a `systemMessage` warning when the hook payload cannot be read, is invalid or non-object JSON, or guard evaluation raises an internal exception.")
  Problem: The §25.D prose enumerates the four fail-open paths that emit a `systemMessage` warning, but it does not document the fifth path that the implementation takes: an empty or whitespace-only stdin is treated as `{}` and allowed silently with no warning. The `main()` body in `.claude/hooks/pr_watch_guard.py` short-circuits with `payload = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}` before `json.loads` runs, so empty input never reaches the `ValueError` branch and never reaches `_warn(...)`. The test `test_malformed_payload_allows_with_warning` (lines 173-183) documents this as intentional behavior with an explicit comment ("An empty payload is a valid (empty) object: nothing to warn about.") and asserts `result.stdout == ""` for `""` and `"   "`. The new regression assertion `test_claude_md_documents_the_rule` (lines 252-256, added in the last run) cements the incomplete text by string-matching the exact warning-only phrasing, so the docs and the test have to be updated together.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is a documentation-versus-behavior mismatch, not a runtime correctness defect. An operator or contributor reading §25.D will conclude that every non-blocked payload path emits a `systemMessage` warning; when an empty or whitespace-only payload arrives (a real possibility during hook initialization or when an MCP wrapper drops its payload), the absence of any warning or block can read as a silent regression of the guard's enforcement posture. Copilot review comment `entry[5]` (id 3954397537) flagged this same gap after the last autofix commit, and the cross-pollination consensus finding from `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `minimax/minimax-m3`, `mistralai/mistral-small-2603`, and `qwen/qwen3.7-plus` reports it at severity ranging from NIT to MAJOR (consensus severity: high). The fix is a small prose clarification in §25.D plus a one-line update to the corresponding assertion in `test_claude_md_documents_the_rule`, e.g. "An empty or whitespace-only payload is treated as `{}` and allowed silently (there is nothing to parse) — the four paths above describe the warning-emitting failure modes only." Behavior is correct; the gap is in the prose the rule contract documents.
  severity=MAJOR
  confidence=5

- CLAUDE.md
  Line or code reference: lines 1465-1469 (§25.D, the sentence "fails open with a `systemMessage` warning when the hook payload cannot be read, is invalid or non-object JSON, or guard evaluation raises an internal exception.")
  Problem: The documented fail-open contract enumerates warning-emitting cases but omits the empty/whitespace-only payload path. The implementation at .claude/hooks/pr_watch_guard.py line 99 (`payload = json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}`) treats an empty or whitespace-only payload as `{}` and allows the call silently — no `systemMessage` warning is emitted. An empty payload is not valid JSON, so a reader of §25.D would expect the "invalid JSON" warning branch to fire, yet `test_malformed_payload_allows_with_warning` in tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py (the `else` branch asserting `result.stdout == ""` for empty/whitespace stdin) explicitly pins the silent-allow behavior. The same omission exists in the hook's own docstring at .claude/hooks/pr_watch_guard.py lines 30-33 and its byte-identical mirror workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_watch_guard.py lines 30-33 ("an unreadable, invalid, or non-object payload, or an internal evaluation error, allows the call with a `systemMessage` warning" — empty payload allows the call with no warning and is not mentioned). This matches Copilot review comment entry[5] at CLAUDE.md:1469, which is still unaddressed in the current diff.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — the hook behavior is intentional and tested. The defect is a documentation-versus-behavior mismatch in a normative policy file that ships verbatim to every consumer repo: an operator auditing §25.D's fail-open contract will be surprised that an empty/whitespace payload produces neither a warning nor a block, and may misdiagnose the silent allow as a malfunction. Fixing the CLAUDE.md sentence requires also updating the exact-text assertion in tests/test_pr_watch_guard.py (test_claude_md_documents_the_rule, the block asserting the verbatim "fails open with a `systemMessage` warning when the hook payload cannot be read, is invalid or non-object JSON, or guard evaluation raises an internal exception." sentence) or that test will fail.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=5
- changelog.d/pr-watch-disabled.md
  Line or code reference: the filename itself (no numeric prefix)
  Problem: CLAUDE.md §20.B mandates the fragment filename format `changelog.d/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` (example `changelog.d/3712-soft-deadline-finalization.md`), where "the number is the issue or PR the work belongs to". This fragment is named `pr-watch-disabled.md` with no issue/PR number, deviating from the documented convention. The assembler (scripts/assemble_changelog.py `iter_fragment_paths`, lines 117-137) accepts any top-level `*.md`, so the entry still ships — the deviation is contract-level, not functional.
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure; the fragment is discovered and folded correctly. The risk is convention drift in a mechanism whose entire design rationale (§20.B: "Never reuse another PR's filename — the unique path is the whole point") depends on disciplined, traceable naming, and future tooling or audits keyed on the `<issue-or-pr>` prefix would skip this entry.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=3
